newsitem.title: USA: Midsize utility vehicles found short on safety.
newsitem.headline: Midsize utility vehicles found short on safety.

text.p: A safety group said on Thursday that after testing two more midsize utility vehicles it still had not found one to which it could give a "best pick" or "good" overall rating for crashworthiness.
The industry-supported Insurance Institute for Highway Safety said the results of a frontal crash test of a Nissan Motor Co. Ltd. Pathfinder were "disappointing."
It said the results of a Mitsubishi Motors Corp. Montero test were better "but still not good."
The group rated Pathfinder crashworthiness "marginal" and Montero's as "acceptable."

Earlier, it gave "acceptable" ratings to these vehicles: the Toyota Motor Corp. 4Runner; the Land Rover Discovery, made by Bayerische Motoren-Werke; and the Ford Motor Co. Explorer/Mercury Mountainer.

It gave a "marginal" rating to the Jeep Grand Cherokee, made by Chrysler Corp., and "poor" ratings to the Isuzu Motors Ltd. Rodeo, the Honda Motor Co. Ltd. Passport, and the Chevrolet Blazer/GMC Jimmy/Oldsmobile Bravada, all made by General Motors Corp.
No vehicle tested got the institute's top rating of "good."
